ghostology: Ghost lore. It seemed even more unaccountable than if it had been a thing of ghostology and witchcraft. Hawthorne.
ghost: 1. The spirit; the soul of man. (old) Then gives her grieved ghost thus to lament. Spenser. 2. The disembodied soul; the soul or spirit of a deceased person; a spirit appearing after death; | To die; to expire. (old) Sir P. Sidney.
ghyll: A ravine. See Gill a woody glen. [Prov. Eng. & Scot.] Wordsworth.
ghastliness: The state of being ghastly; a deathlike look.
ghibelline: One of a faction in Italy, in the 12th and 13th centuries, which favored the German emperors, and opposed the Guelfs, or adherents of the poses. Brande & C.
ghastly: 1. Like a ghost in appearance; deathlike; pale; pallid; dismal. Each turned his face with a ghastly pang. Coleridge. His face was so ghastly that it could scarcely be recognized. Macaulay. 2. | In a ghastly manner; hideously. Staring full ghastly like a strangled man. Shak.
ghast: To strike aghast; to affright. (old) Ghasted by the noise I made. Full suddenly he fled. Shak.
ghebre: A worshiper of fire; a Zoroastrian; a Parsee.
ghetto: The Jews'quarter in an Italian town or city. I went to the Ghetto, where the Jews dwell. Evelyn.
ghostly: 1. Relating to the soul; not carnal or secular; spiritual; as, a ghostly confessor. Save and defend us from our ghostly enemies. Book of Common Prayer [Ch. of Eng. ] One of the gostly children of St. | Spiritually; mystically. Chaucer.
ghawazi: Egyptian dancing girls, of a lower sort than the almeh.
ghastful: Fit to make one aghast; dismal. (old) -- Ghast"ful*ly, adv.
ghazal: A kind of Oriental lyric, and usually erotic, poetry, written in recurring rhymes.
ghostfish: A pale ubspotted variety of the wrymouth.
ghat: 1. A pass through a mountain. [India] J. D. Hooker. 2. A range of mountains. Balfour (Cyc. of Ind. ). 3. Stairs descending to a river; a landing place; a wharf. [India] Malcom.
ghaut: 1. A pass through a mountain. [India] J. D. Hooker. 2. A range of mountains. Balfour (Cyc. of Ind. ). 3. Stairs descending to a river; a landing place; a wharf. [India] Malcom.
ghazel: A kind of Oriental lyric, and usually erotic, poetry, written in recurring rhymes.
gherkin: 1. (Bot.) A kind of small, prickly cucumber, much used for pickles. 2. (Zoöl.) See Sea gherkin.
ghazi: Among Mohammedans, a warrior champion or veteran, esp. in the destruction of infidels.
ghoul: An imaginary evil being among Eastern nations, which was supposed to feed upon human bodies. [Written also ghole .] Moore.
gheber: A worshiper of fire; a Zoroastrian; a Parsee.
ghee: Butter clarified by boiling, and thus converted into a kind of oil. [India] Malcom.
ghoulish: Characteristic of a ghoul; vampirelike; hyenalike.
ghostdance: A religious dance of the North American Indians, participated in by both sexes, and looked upon as a rite of invocation the purpose of which is, through trance and vision, to bring the dancer into communion with the unseen world and the spirits of departed friends.
